en: I bow to you, Dattātreya; be gracious. You are the soul of all and the creator of all; no one knows your limit, O God above all gods. Forgive my offenses, whether known or unknown to you. || 1 ||
O Self, because you are my source of birth and because my intellect is dependent upon you, you alone are to be saluted and worshipped by me;
nevertheless, forgive me for not having offered you remembrance due to my delusion, O Great-Souled One who acts for the welfare of others.

Alas, those like me— destitute of vision and utterly deluded— abandoning this kinsman who bestows both worldly enjoyment and liberation, who is a friend to the distressed and an ocean of compassion, go in search of another for their own welfare.
Though there may be no evildoer equal to me, yet there is no remover of sin equal to you;
O Noble One, there is no one more deserving of compassion than I, nor is there anywhere a supreme compassionate one like you. (4)
O Lord of the helpless, kinsman of the most wretched, O Śrīśa, ocean filled with the nectar of compassion!
[Grant me] devotion to Your feet, the state of being a servant to Your servants, and firm, singular dedication to the meaning of Your mantra. (5)

Grant me the remembrance of the Guru, stainless intellect, and the destruction of mental anguish and physical disease; grant me victory, the accomplishment of desired aims, the subjugation of excellent people, the increase of wealth and food, and the abundance of noble cattle.
O Lord of the body, grant me the attainment of sons and other blessings, as well as nobility; may there be fearlessness for me from all sides.
Salutations to Brahmā, Agni, and the Earth; salutations to the medicinal herbs, to Vāc, and to Viṣṇu, the Lord of Speech.
May the earth be peaceful for us; may the atmosphere and the heavens be auspicious; may the quarters of space be free from fear and auspicious for us.
May the waters and the lightning protect us; O gods, may there be safety for me from all sides—peace!
Thus ends the "Hymn for Seeking Pardon for Offenses Against Datta," composed by Śrī Vāsudevānanda Sarasvatī.
